svg.title: When the next breath comes before the lung has emptied, with zero applied PEEP
svg.desc: Idealized passive linear model with illustrative numbers, not patient data; zero applied PEEP and relaxed respiratory muscles throughout, so the airway opening rests at 0, all volume above FRC is trapped gas, and total PEEP equals intrinsic PEEP; pressures in cm H2O relative to atmospheric pressure at the airway opening. Panel A plots the volume of a slow unit above its relaxed volume, FRC, in mL per 100 mL entering each breath, against time, with 3 seconds per breath. In the top trace, with enough time, every exhalation returns to the dashed FRC line. In the bottom trace, with 2 seconds to exhale and a 2.5 second time constant, each exhalation is cut short, so end-expiratory volume climbs in shrinking steps of +45, +20, +9, +4 and +2, to 45, 65, 74, 78 and 80 mL, approaching a new plateau of about 82 mL drawn as a dotted line; the trapped volume above FRC is hatched. A note adds that with 5 seconds to exhale the plateau is about 16 mL. Panel B shows the start of one breath with intrinsic PEEP of 10, which with zero applied PEEP is also the total PEEP, as three traces on a shared time axis of about 1 second. Alveolar pressure starts at +10 and falls steadily through the dashed airway-opening line at 0 to slightly below 0. Flow starts below the zero line, labeled expiratory flow still present, reaches zero as alveolar pressure reaches 0, and only then becomes inspiratory. Volume falls slightly, is flat as flow crosses zero, then rises once inspiratory flow begins. A hatched band over the first half second marks the threshold: pressure without volume change, effort and energy spent, almost no mechanical work. Under the heading pressure requirement is not work, a solid box gives the simplified, elastic-only pressure requirement at a compliance of 0.05 L/cm H2O: intrinsic PEEP 10 plus 10 for the breath, a peak of 20 cm H2O versus 10. A dashed box, labeled a different quantity, gives work as pressure times volume change: elastic work rises from 2.5 to 7.5 cm H2O·L, 0.25 to 0.74 J, with resistive work not shown. A note for a ventilated patient with a pressure trigger set 2 below airway-opening pressure and zero applied PEEP gives the effort needed as about 10 plus 2, or 12 cm H2O. A terms strip defines dynamic hyperinflation as volume trapped at end-expiration, which equals volume above FRC only when applied PEEP is zero and the respiratory muscles are relaxed; intrinsic PEEP as the recoil pressure from that trapped volume at end-expiration; applied PEEP as pressure set at the airway opening; and total PEEP as what an end-expiratory hold reads, applied plus intrinsic, so that with nonzero applied PEEP, intrinsic PEEP is the hold reading minus the applied PEEP.
